name: OpenChamber
summary: Your OpenChamber sessions, approvals and usage in the notch
description:
OpenChamber puts the coding sessions you run in OpenChamber beside the notch. The shelf widget says what each one is doing in plain words, such as Running swift test or Editing Views.swift, with its model and reasoning level, agent profile and server, how full its context window is, and how long the turn has run; while the agent writes, its words appear as it writes them. Several sessions show at once: click one to open it in place, hover what it is doing to read the whole command and its last message, or expand it over the whole shelf to see every step of the turn, its full last message, and Stop.

When a session asks for permission, a card appears on the notch with the exact command, and you allow it once or reject it without leaving what you are doing; the widget keeps every pending request, with Always for the ones you trust. A question with a short list of answers is answered from its card too. Cards also tell you when a turn ends, with how many lines and files it changed, or fails, unless OpenChamber is already in front.

The widget's Usage page shows a ring per provider with what is left of its tightest window, a mark where an even pace would be, when a window will run out before it resets, every window on hover, and a notice as one passes 80% and 95%. With nothing running, the widget shows what your agents did today. Beside the notch, the agent's own mascot works while it does, with a dot for each running session.

It watches every server OpenChamber Desktop on this Mac is set up for, this Mac's own and your remote hosts, directly or through OpenChamber's relay, using the tokens Desktop already has, so there is nothing to pair.
